question_text: Differentiate between mature B-cells and functional B-cells.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Mature B-cells
steps.why: A mature B cell carries its antibody on the outside but has not yet met an antigen, so it is ready but not yet working.
common_mistakes: Writing that mature B cells release antibodies. They display them.
Placing them in the lymph nodes. They are made in the bone marrow.
steps.memory_tip: Mature in the marrow, functional in the lymph organs.
steps.margin_note: Two rows: where made, what it does.
lines: Mature B-cells are produced from stem
cells in the bone marrow of adult mammals.
They make antibodies which are displayed on

steps.label: Functional B-cells
steps.why: Once it reaches a lymphoid organ and meets its antigen, the cell divides into one kind that fights now and one that remembers.
common_mistakes: Saying functional B cells are made in the marrow. They develop from mature B cells.
Naming only one of the two products.
steps.memory_tip: Functional B cells split into memory cells and plasma cells.
steps.margin_note: Both products are marked. Name them.

lines.text: They become memory cells and plasma cells

insider_note: The difference is WHERE each is found and WHAT it becomes. Bone marrow for the mature cell, secondary lymphoid organs for the functional one.
